name: Troitsk
summary: Troitsk nu-mass uses a windowless gaseous tritium source and electrostatic spectroscopy at INR RAS near Moscow. Its completed endpoint-mass dataset was followed by a sterile-neutrino programme and silicon-detector development, so the facility did not end with the 1994-2004 mass measurements.
physics_targets: Sterile-neutrino admixtures in tritium beta decay
detection_principle: A windowless gaseous tritium source emits beta electrons into a MAC-E spectrometer. The historical endpoint analysis constrained the effective neutrino mass; later integral and differential spectrum measurements with silicon drift detectors search for additional neutrino mass eigenstates.

status.label: Completed mass dataset / continuing detector research
status.evidence: The 1994-2004 standard-mass dataset is complete. Subsequent sterile-neutrino measurements used a TRISTAN prototype detector, while the INR facility page describes continuing detector development and plans for measurement sessions in May and autumn 2026; the schedule alone does not confirm that those sessions occurred.

phases.name: Endpoint neutrino-mass campaign
phases.description: The standard-mass result uses data collected during 1994-2004 and reanalysed in 2011.

phases.name: Sterile-neutrino searches and detector development
phases.description: Integral and differential beta-spectrum measurements continued with prototype silicon drift detectors. The facility advertises further research and measurement plans for 2026.

results.summary: The reanalysis reported a mass-squared result consistent with zero and an upper bound on the effective neutrino mass.
A seven-pixel TRISTAN prototype enabled integral and differential beta-spectrum measurements and reported sterile-neutrino mixing limits over mass ranges extending to about 6 keV.

science_scope: This is a laboratory kinematic measurement of the effective electron-flavour neutrino mass. Its observable differs from the effective Majorana mass in neutrinoless double-beta decay and the sum of neutrino masses inferred from cosmology.
